_note: Official proof-of-funds (living costs) amounts for student visas. Update when governments change them. Amounts exclude tuition unless stated.

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: 12-month living-cost amount for the primary student applicant (Student visa subclass 500).
countries.plus: Add first-year tuition and return travel costs; more for a partner or children.

source.label: Department of Home Affairs — Student visa (subclass 500)

countries.notes: Amount as listed by Home Affairs and widely reported; check the official page before applying.

countries.name: Austria
countries.summary: 2026 amounts: €722.58 a month if you are under 24, €1,308.39 if you are 24 or older, shown for 12 months in advance.
countries.plus: If rent is above €386.43 a month, add the difference. Add health insurance (student insurance about €78.84 a month).

source.label: OeAD — Residence permit: student

countries.name: Belgium
countries.summary: Minimum net amount per month for the 2026-27 academic year, usually shown for 12 months (for example through a blocked account).
countries.plus: Tuition is separate. Indexed every year.

source.label: Belgian Immigration Office — sufficient means of subsistence

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.summary: No fixed amount is published. You must prove sufficient resources for your stay.
countries.plus: Ask your university for the exact amount.

source.label: European Commission — EU Immigration Portal: student in Bulgaria

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Minimum living expenses for a single applicant studying outside Quebec, for study permit applications made on or after 1 September 2026. Quebec has its own amounts.
countries.plus: Add first-year tuition and travel costs. Bringing family increases the amount.

source.label: IRCC — Study permit: proof of financial support

countries.notes: Amount confirmed from IRCC's 28 August 2026 update as reported by CIC News; check IRCC's page before applying.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.summary: At least €362.75 a month plus €870.60 for travel costs.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: University of Zagreb — visa and stay information

countries.notes: Amount as published by the University of Zagreb (December 2025); confirm with the Croatian police.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.summary: No fixed amount is published by the Migration Department. Universities usually ask for a bank statement and a bank guarantee.
countries.plus: Ask your university's international office for the exact amount.

source.label: Civil Registry and Migration Department

countries.name: Czechia
countries.summary: 15 × the subsistence minimum (CZK 3,130) for the first month — CZK 46,950 — plus CZK 6,260 for each further month.
countries.plus: Applicants under 18 show half.

source.label: Czech Embassy — long-term visa for study

countries.name: Denmark
countries.summary: Only if you are NOT paying tuition (e.g. tuition waiver): DKK 7,426 a month (2026), up to 12 months. If you have paid tuition, no extra proof is needed.
countries.plus: Family members need extra funds.

source.label: SIRI — financial self-support

countries.name: Estonia
countries.summary: Sufficient legal income of at least €880 a month (2026).
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: Police and Border Guard Board — student guide (2026)

countries.name: Finland
countries.summary: €800 a month. For a permit of a year or longer you must have €9,600 in your bank account when you apply.
countries.plus: Unpaid tuition must also be in your account.

source.label: Migri — income requirement for students

countries.name: France
countries.summary: At least €615 a month — the basic allowance paid to French government scholarship holders.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate. Some renewal pages from the French administration show a higher figure (€877.50 a month), so check France-Visas for your case.

source.label: European Commission — EU Immigration Portal: student in France

countries.notes: Official sources show different figures for first visas and renewals.

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: Proof of financial resources, usually through a blocked account (Sperrkonto). Only the monthly amount can be withdrawn after arrival.
countries.plus: Tuition (if any) and health insurance are separate.

source.label: German Federal Foreign Office — blocked account

countries.name: Greece
countries.summary: At least €650 a month for the period of the residence permit.
countries.plus: Older Greek Foreign Ministry documents still show €400 — check with the embassy.

source.label: University of Athens — visa and residence permit

countries.name: Hungary
countries.summary: No fixed amount is published. You must show enough money for your stay, accommodation and return journey, with bank statements or a scholarship.
countries.plus: Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship holders follow their scholarship's rules.

source.label: National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing — students

countries.name: Iceland
countries.summary: ISK 259,951 a month from 18 May 2026, secured for as long as the permit is valid.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: Directorate of Immigration — higher means of support

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: Immediate access to at least €10,000 for a one-year course, and the same for each later year.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: Irish Immigration Service — student finances

countries.name: Italy
countries.summary: Annual means of subsistence for a study visa (Type D), set by the Ministry of University and Research procedures for 2026-27 and 2027-28. Funds must be lawful and traceable, preferably your own or your family's.
countries.plus: Tuition and accommodation are separate.

source.label: MUR procedures for international students 2026-27 and 2027-28

countries.name: Latvia
countries.summary: €500 a month (plus €150 a month for each child who comes with you).
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: PMLP — residence permit for studies

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.summary: Half the minimum monthly wage (€577 in 2026) for each month, for at least one year, plus one minimum wage (€1,153) for the return journey.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: Vilnius University — visa and residence permit

countries.notes: Amounts as published by Vilnius University from the Migration Department rule.

countries.name: Malta
countries.summary: 75% of the national minimum wage for every month of study — about €745.68 a month in 2026 (minimum wage €229.44 a week).
countries.plus: The minimum wage rises in January 2027, so the amount will go up.

source.label: Identità — student national visa document list

countries.notes: Monthly figure calculated by us from the official rule (75% of minimum wage).

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.summary: The 'study norm' for university and HBO students in 2026 — usually 12 months' worth deposited with your university.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate. The amount changes every 1 January.

source.label: IND — required amounts (study)

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.summary: NZD 20,000 for each year of tertiary study, or NZD 1,667 per month if your study is shorter than a year.
countries.plus: Tuition and outward travel are separate.

source.label: Immigration New Zealand — student fund requirements

countries.name: Norway
countries.summary: NOK 170,368 for the 2026-27 academic year (NOK 15,488 a month).
countries.plus: One semester only: NOK 77,440 (autumn) or NOK 92,928 (spring). Tuition is separate.

source.label: UDI — study permit

countries.name: Poland
countries.summary: At least PLN 776 a month for living costs, plus accommodation costs and money for a return ticket (PLN 2,500 from outside Europe).
countries.plus: Add your rent for each month and your tuition.

source.label: Polish government — student visa information

countries.name: Portugal
countries.summary: Means of subsistence equal to the national minimum wage for each month of study — €920 a month in 2026.
countries.plus: Less may be needed if housing or meals are covered. Nationals of Portuguese-speaking (CPLP) countries admitted to a university are exempt.

source.label: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs — visa legislation

countries.notes: Amount follows Portugal's 2026 minimum wage; confirm on the official visa portal.

countries.name: Romania
countries.summary: At least the gross minimum wage for each month of the visa — RON 4,325 a month from 1 July 2026.
countries.plus: You must also prove one year of tuition is paid.

source.label: European Commission — EU Immigration Portal: student in Romania

countries.notes: Rule from the official portal; RON 4,325 is the minimum wage reported by EURES from 1 July 2026.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.summary: The subsistence minimum (€295.22 from July 2026) for each month; for stays over a year, 12 times that amount.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: EURAXESS Slovakia — residence information

countries.notes: Figure from the Slovak Academy of Sciences' EURAXESS office; confirm with the Foreign Police.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.summary: At least Slovenia's basic minimum income — currently €507.43 a month.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate.

source.label: University of Ljubljana — residence permit for studies

countries.notes: Amount as published by the University of Ljubljana; confirm with the administrative unit.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.summary: No single national figure. Universities and embassies set it — many ask for about USD 20,000 (or KRW 20 million) for a D-2 degree visa.
countries.plus: Check your university's visa guide and your embassy.

source.label: Study in Korea (NIIED)

countries.name: Spain
countries.summary: 100% of IPREM (Spain's public income indicator) for each month of your stay — €600 a month in 2026.
countries.plus: Tuition is separate. Family members add 75% (first) and 50% (each other) of IPREM.

source.label: Spanish Consulate — study visa

countries.notes: Consulates state the amount differently; check your own consulate's page.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.summary: At least SEK 10,656 a month (applications in 2026) for the whole period of the permit.
countries.plus: Less if your university gives you free housing or food. Tuition is separate.

source.label: Swedish Migration Agency — maintenance requirement

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.summary: No national amount — each canton sets its own. Zurich asks for CHF 21,000 a year; other cantons differ.
countries.plus: Tuition and health insurance are separate.

source.label: University of Zurich — entry guidelines

countries.notes: Zurich figure; check the migration office of your canton.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Money to support yourself for up to 9 months, plus the first year's course fees shown on your CAS. Not needed if you have been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months.
countries.plus: Add your first-year course fees (minus anything already paid).

source.label: GOV.UK — Student visa: money you need

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: No fixed government amount. Your university sets the cost of attendance (tuition + living costs) on your Form I-20, and you must prove funds for at least the first year.
countries.plus: Use the total on your I-20.

source.label: Study in the States (DHS) — financial ability
